observations: ct-tabs renders no images/icons of its own. Non-text content lives inside whatever a ct-tabs-item's slotted panel body contains and is that content's own responsibility.

standard: 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (Level A)

observations: The tablist/tab/tabpanel relationship is established programmatically by the component itself, not left to the implementer: the tablist container gets role="tablist", each trigger gets role="tab" plus aria-selected/aria-controls, and each panel gets role="tabpanel" plus aria-labelledby pointing back at its trigger — all wired automatically via the Zag.js tabs machine's connect() output (see tabs.ts's renderTrigger()/renderPanel()). No manual id/aria wiring is required from the implementer supplying ct-tabs-item children.

Tabs and panels are rendered in the same order as the ct-tabs-item light-DOM children were supplied; neither the tablist (ct-item-list, gap/layout only) nor the panel wrapper uses the CSS `order` property to reassign visual order away from DOM order.
The tablist is always horizontal (matching upstream CivicTheme, which has no vertical tabs variant); content is not restricted to a single display orientation.
ct-tabs renders no form inputs.

The selected tab is conveyed through aria-selected (exposed to assistive technology) plus a distinct background/border color and its data-selected attribute — not through color alone. A sighted user without color perception can still tell the selected tab apart by its raised/joined-to-the-panel border shape (upstream's --ct-tabs-link-border-radius top corners plus the collapsed bottom border), not solely by the active background-color swap.

Both themes were verified against civictheme.variables.css-sourced tokens: light theme trigger text is --ct-color-light-body on --ct-tabs-light-links-background-color (aliasing --ct-color-light-background); dark theme trigger text is --ct-color-dark-body on --ct-tabs-dark-links-background-color (aliasing --ct-color-dark-background). Both pairings reuse the same body-text-on-background combination already verified elsewhere in this token set (e.g. ct-accordion, ct-popover) and comfortably exceed 4.5:1.
No fixed-height/overflow:hidden container clips trigger or panel text at 200% zoom; the tablist (ct-item-list) wraps via flex-wrap rather than truncating when trigger labels grow.
ct-tabs renders no images of text itself; compliance depends on the implementer not embedding an image-of-text into a ct-tabs-item's slotted panel content.

The tablist reuses ct-item-list's flex-wrap: wrap layout, so triggers reflow onto additional lines at narrow/zoomed viewports instead of requiring two-dimensional scrolling; panels have no fixed width.

Both themes' trigger borders (--ct-tabs-light/dark-links-border-color, aliasing --ct-color-*-border-light) and the focus-visible outline (--ct-outline-width/--ct-outline-light/--ct-outline-dark, the same token pair already verified for ct-link/ct-accordion) meet the 3:1 minimum against their adjacent background.
No fixed-height container on either the trigger or the panel clips text when line/letter/word spacing is increased per the criterion's multipliers.

standard: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA)
observations: Panels are click/keyboard-activation-triggered only (a real aria-selected state change from TAB_CLICK or Enter/Space), never shown merely as a side effect of hover or focus — unlike ct-tooltip's hover/focus-triggered content, this criterion's hover/focus-triggered-content requirements do not apply.

Every trigger is a real native <button role="tab">, reachable via Tab (only the selected trigger is in the Tab order at any time — a roving tabindex, the standard ARIA authoring-practices tablist pattern) and operable via Enter or Space (native button activation) or a mouse/pointer click. Once a trigger has focus, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move focus between tabs and Home/End jump to the first/last — all provided by the Zag.js tabs machine's getListProps().onKeyDown, unmodified.
Nothing in the tablist or panel traps focus; Tab moves past the single selected trigger and into/out of the visible panel's content normally.

No single-character key shortcuts are implemented; arrow/Home/End are all standard multi-key or modifier-free navigation keys expected for the tablist pattern, not single-character shortcuts in the criterion's sense.
Tab selection has no auto-advance timer of any kind; a tab stays selected until the user explicitly activates a different one.

standard: 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (Level A)

observations: Focus order follows DOM order (tablist triggers, in the order ct-tabs-item children were supplied, then the visible panel's content); the roving tabindex only changes which single trigger is a Tab stop, never the relative order of focusable elements.

ct-tabs renders no links of its own — triggers are native <button> elements, not anchors (see tabs.ts's doc comment on why ct-link is not composed for the trigger); link purpose within a panel's slotted content is that content's own responsibility.

Compliance depends on the implementer providing a clear, descriptive `heading` for each ct-tabs-item (e.g. "Eligibility", not "Tab 2"). This is real in principle, but — same structural gap already documented in accordion.a11y-conditional.e2e.ts/heading.a11y-conditional.e2e.ts — the mechanical rules.mjs 2.4.6 extractor only evaluates `label`/`legend` element text, never a `<button>`'s, so it is not reachable by the enforced conditional test tier; see tabs.a11y-conditional.e2e.ts's header comment.
The trigger button's own :focus-visible outline (--ct-outline-width/--ct-outline-light/--ct-outline-dark) is always present regardless of implementer input.
ct-tabs introduces no floating/overlapping content of its own that could obscure a focused trigger; the visible panel is a normal in-flow block below the tablist.
Only a simple pointer click is used to activate a tab; no multipoint or path-based gesture.
Selection changes on click completion (the native button's click event, which the Zag machine's TAB_CLICK handler responds to), not on an unabortable pointerdown.

ct-tabs-item exposes no aria-label override for the trigger, so a trigger's accessible name is always exactly its visible `heading` text — there is no way through this component's public API to set a mismatching accessible name.

Trigger padding (0.5rem/0.75rem vertical plus 1rem horizontal, per upstream tabs.css) generally yields a comfortable target, but compliance for a very short single-character `heading` in isolation depends on the implementer providing sufficiently descriptive (and thus wider) tab labels.
The document's lang attribute is outside this component's scope.
Compliance depends on the implementer setting a lang attribute on a `heading` or panel content whose language differs from the surrounding page.

Focusing a trigger alone does not select it — manual activation mode (matching upstream tabs.js's click-only vanilla behavior) requires an explicit click or Enter/Space activation — so no unexpected change of context occurs purely as a result of arrow-key-driven focus movement.
Switching the visible panel is a direct, expected result of activating a trigger, not an unexpected side effect of some other input.
Compliance depends on the implementer using the same tab `heading` wording for tabs serving the same purpose wherever ct-tabs recurs across a site.
ct-tabs has no form-validation role.
ct-tabs is not a form input.

The Zag.js machine provides role/state wiring automatically (role="tablist"/"tab"/"tabpanel", aria-selected, aria-controls/aria-labelledby, aria-disabled on a disabled tab) unconditionally — but each trigger's accessible name still depends on the implementer supplying a non-empty `heading`; `heading` is required in TabsItemSchema, but the Lit component does not enforce a non-empty value at runtime (same caveat already documented for ct-accordion-item's `heading`, ct-popover's `triggerText`, ct-tooltip's `label`).
Switching the visible panel is a direct result of the user's own click/keyboard activation of a visible control, not an out-of-band status update requiring an aria-live region.
